hypotheses.construction_plan: Distribute x in the first argument to write x*(y+z)=x*y+x*z. Then both F-arguments are evaluations of the common kernel F(a*y+b*z): the first is K(x,x), the second is K(x,w).
hypotheses.rationale: The two F arguments are linear forms in the same variables y,z with the same y-coefficient x and different z-coefficients x and w, so a single bilinear kernel explains both.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Define the linear-in-t family P(t)=t*(y+z). Evaluating at t=x gives x*(y+z); differentiating with respect to t gives y+z.
required_assumptions: y and z are independent of t
hypotheses.rationale: The observed derivative relation is generated by a one-parameter linear family in the multiplier of the sum y+z.
